ledger.claim: The trip record shows no driver arrival at all: arrived_at is null and started_at is null, so limb (a) of POL-NS-01 — a driver 'arrived' event in the trip_record — fails on its face, and the no-show fee is not chargeable under the anchor clause.

The driver's own GPS trace never places him within the arrival radius for this zone class: across 55 driver fixes the qualifying in-radius fix count is 0 against the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, so the POL-NS-02 proximity test — at least 3 consecutive fixes inside the radius — is not met and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee.

The wrong-entrance doctrine in POL-NS-03 cannot rescue the charge: that clause's outer ceiling is 400 m measured from trip_record.pickup, and the driver's closest approach to the pin across the whole trace was 2240.04 m — more than five times the ceiling — so the driver was not at the pickup point in any sense the policy recognises.

Even if arrival were somehow taken as established, the effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum, a 300-second shortfall, and POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation fee in full whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages.

The accumulation route in POL-NS-06(i) is not open to the driver: the limb requires a traffic_advisory that is present and populated, covering the pickup road and in force over the wait, and EV-ADVIS-00610-01 is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0. The absence itself is citable, and limb (i) is simply unavailable rather than exonerating anyone.

No waiting clock ever ran: the driver's trace shows continuous motion at distinct speeds of 71.1 to 74.1 kph across a 3.74 km trace — far above the 15 kph motion threshold POL-NS-05 uses to distinguish a held position from a vehicle in motion — so there is no stationary wait for any fee to compensate. Considered under POL-NS-05 limb (ii), there is no qualifying in-geofence fix anywhere in the trip, and the fee is refunded in full with no compensation payable.

Limb (d) of POL-NS-01 fails independently of the arrival tests: the trip was terminated with cancellation_reason_code OTHER — not RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT — so the record does not carry the no-show ground the clause requires.

The driver's own contemporaneous message admits the cancellation was driver-caused — 'accident, cannot come, pls cancel from your side' — and his counterparty statement confirms he was in a collision and asked the passenger to cancel. A driver who tells the rider he cannot perform the trip and asks her to cancel cannot found a rider no-show charge on that same cancellation.

No driver compensation is payable on this trip: POL-NS-07 pays 80 percent of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not satisfied on any limb — no arrival event, no qualifying in-geofence fix, no dwell, and no recognised no-show reason code.

Escalation must not swallow this refund. On the tests POL-NS-09 names: rider and driver have 0 counterparty disputes in the trailing 90 days under limb (c), rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 under limb (d), and on the POL-NS-07 anti-farming test driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 against completed_trips_30d of 110 — nowhere near the 4-and-0.08 thresholds. The artifacts that carry the deciding facts (trip record, GPS trace, fare breakdown) are all COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so nothing caps confidence below the 0.70 floor.

The driver's own device trace places him no closer than 2,240 m to the pickup pin at any point in the trace, and his recorded fix-to-fix speeds run between roughly 71 and 74 km/h throughout — he was never at or near the pickup point. The trip record carries no 'arrived' event at all (trip_record.arrived_at is null), and the termination is recorded as a RIDER cancellation with cancellation_reason_code OTHER, which is not one of the three codes POL-NS-01 limb (d) recognises. Limbs (a), (b) and (d) of POL-NS-01 therefore cannot be made out on this record, and the driver does not contend that the SGD 4.00 fee is chargeable under POL-NS-01. What the driver asks is that the ruling reflect the record rather than a scheme: on a trace with no qualifying in-radius fix under POL-NS-02, the fee is refundable to the rider, and that is the disposition the driver accepts.

The driver must not be tagged with a false-arrival finding. POL-NS-05 fires only where the trip record carries an 'arrived' event with a timestamp that the GPS trace then contradicts, and the false-arrival record and referral in POL-NS-05(ii) follow only from that trigger. Here trip_record.arrived_at is null: no arrival marker was tapped at all, so the clause is not engaged and no POL-NS-05(ii) false-arrival referral should be recorded against this driver. He told the rider in the in-app message at 17:50:40, 'accident, cannot come, pls cancel from your side', and repeated the same account in his counterparty statement — this is a driver who said he could not complete the trip, not one who farmed a no-show fee.

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming guard is not tripped and no escalation follows from the parties' profiles. The check requires BOTH limbs: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d must be 4 or more (it is 1) AND that figure divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d must exceed 0.08 (1/110 is 0.009). Neither limb holds, so there is no basis to withhold compensation on that ground under POL-NS-07 or to escalate under POL-NS-09(d). The same is true of the repeat-dealing trigger: rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0. The trailing-window counters are the operative ones here, and every one of them is clean.

No part of this case turns on the amount charged, and no fare-integrity impairment can be built on it. The SGD 4.00 cancellation-fee line on the ledger is exactly what fee_schedule.resolution_rule produces for this trip: the STANDARD zone-class fee is SGD 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee is SGD 4.00, and the greater of the two is SGD 4.00. The fare line therefore reconciles with the schedule and there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect — the dispute is about chargeability, not arithmetic, and the driver does not dispute the figure.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee charged on 10 September 2026 is refunded to the rider in full, and no compensation is paid to the driver.

Why the fee does not stand. Under POL-NS-01 a no-show fee is chargeable only if all four conditions hold, and none does. (a) The trip record contains no driver 'arrived' event — arrived_at is null and started_at is null. (b) The GPS trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix: 0 of the driver's 55 fixes fall within the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and his closest approach to the pickup pin anywhere in the trace was 2,240.04 m. (c) In-geofence dwell is 0 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum. (d) The trip was terminated by the rider with cancellation_reason_code OTHER, which is not one of RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT. All four limbs fail on the record, and neither advocate contends otherwise.

This drives a full refund under POL-NS-02: where the GPS trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix at any point in the 15 minutes before the 17:54:40 cancellation, the driver never arrived and the rider is entitled to the fee back. POL-NS-03 does not rescue the charge — its 400 m ceiling, measured from trip_record.pickup, is not remotely approached, the driver's minimum distance being 2,240.04 m. POL-NS-06 reaches the same result independently: effective in-geofence dwell of 0 seconds against a 300-second minimum, a 300-second shortfall; the accumulation route in limb (i) is unavailable because EV-ADVIS-00610-01 is MISSING (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0), and a MISSING advisory cannot be asserted to excuse a shortfall.

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 pays 80 percent of the fee — SGD 3.20 of SGD 4.00 — only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not satisfied on any limb. The POL-NS-03(ii) pin-ambiguity goodwill of SGD 2.00 also does not apply: it requires the driver to have been stationary for the required dwell within 400 m of the pin and registered_pickup_points of 2 or more, whereas the driver was over 2,240 m away and registered_pickup_points is 1.

No false-arrival referral is recorded against the driver. POL-NS-05(ii) records a false-arrival event only where an 'arrived' event exists and the GPS contradicts its timestamp; no arrival marker was tapped at all, so the clause is not engaged. The driver's own in-app message at 17:50:40 ('accident, cannot come, pls cancel from your side') and his statement are an admission that he could not perform the trip, not fee-farming; his account and the telemetry agree, and he did not harvest a fee.

Escalation tests. driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 (threshold 4) and 1/110 = 0.009 (threshold 0.08) — the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check is not tripped. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, and disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both profiles, so POL-NS-09(c) and (d) do not fire. No POL-NS-08 impairment applies either: there is no 'arrived'-event clock skew, no trace gap (max_gap 0 s across 55 fixes, rider track present), chat_message_count matches the single logged message, and the SGD 4.00 fee line reconciles with fee_schedule.resolution_rule — the greater of the STANDARD zone fee SGD 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee SGD 4.00, a tie at SGD 4.00. No escalation trigger under POL-NS-09 fires.

Amount. The charge is the SGD 4.00 cancellation-fee line on EV-FARE-00610; base fare, distance, time, ERP, waiting and platform fees are all 0.00, so total_charged is SGD 4.00, and that is the figure refunded.

Confidence. The deciding facts — that no arrival event was recorded and that no qualifying in-radius fix exists — are carried by the trip record and the GPS trace, both COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 and independent of each other; the confidence cap is therefore 1.0, well above the 0.70 escalation floor, so the case does not escalate. The only sub-1.0 artifact, the MISSING traffic advisory at weight 0.0, carries no fact and is relied on only for its absence.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
